summary: Gone Fremont County, Wyoming, tower 20 miles northwest of Dubois; sources give no build date, and a secondhand 1965 account names an observer until 1921.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Wyoming list; no removal date in the sources

staffing.status: last recorded observer Mont Collom, at least until 1921

facts.agency: Shoshone National Forest; Forest Lookouts also lists Washakie National Forest

events.note: Mont Collom was the lookout each summer at least until 1921, when Mr. Bayer left the district

evidence.supports: location about 20 miles northwest of Dubois
Washakie National Forest, then Shoshone National Forest
evidence.quote: Washakie National Forest > Shoshone National Forest

evidence.supports: interview with Charlie Bayer dated October 21, 1965
evidence.quote: October 21, 1965: From an interview with Charlie Bayer in The Pinedale Roundup

evidence.supports: Mont Collom as fire observer on the Pinnacle Butte lookout
evidence.quote: was the fire observer on the lookout station on Pinnacle Butte

evidence.supports: Mont Collom an art and music teacher at Lander High School
evidence.quote: Mont Collom an Art and Music teacher at Lander High School

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives only the Shoshone National Forest; Forest Lookouts gives the Washakie National Forest and then the Shoshone National Forest. Both are kept.

notes_for_editor: No build date, design, height or removal date appears in any source read. Staffing rests on a secondhand 1965 interview as quoted by Forest Lookouts. The Wikipedia article on Pinnacle Buttes covers the mountain, not the lookout. Two web searches found no other lookout history. Guessed firetower.org registry URL returned 404; no registry entry was located. Brief's agency entry (Washakie National Forest) matches only one of the two names in sources; the story reports both. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Lander High School wording was added to evidence, and the Collom sentence was reworded so it no longer copies the quote.
